headline: Perennial highlights Australia's 'duck curve' solar advantage as a structural cost benefit for energy-intensive industrial processes.
reasoning: Australia's exceptional solar resource floods the grid at midday, pushing electricity prices to near zero or even negative — a phenomenon known as the duck curve. Perennial argues that companies can exploit this window for energy-intensive industrial processes, accessing near-zero-cost grid energy and structurally lowering operating costs. The trade-off is higher upfront capital expenditure versus lower and more predictable ongoing costs, which Perennial frames as a net positive for balance sheet resilience and national energy security. Electrification and the use of domestic renewable electricity is presented as both a financial and strategic imperative.

This is Australia's structural advantage, where companies can utilize this window for energy intensive industrial processes and access near zero cost grid energy during the day. The trade-off is between higher upfront capital costs with low operating costs, versus lower initial outlay but rising and volatile ongoing costs. This kind of OpEx over CapEx logic protects balance sheets in the short term but ultimately transfers and amplifies the cost onto the Australian taxpayer.

headline: Perennial overweight transition metals on structural demand/supply imbalance driven by global energy transition
reasoning: The trust holds an overweight position in companies exposed to transition metals such as copper, lithium, cobalt and rare earths, where the demand outlook is very strong. Given the long – and increasing – delays in developing new mines, it is likely that demand will significantly exceed supply over the coming years. Further, the 'low-hanging fruit' of shallow, easily accessed deposits of most minerals have been mined first (some of the world's largest copper mines, for example Rio's Bingham Canyon mine in Utah, are over 100 years old!) and new mines are often in more 'challenging' locations (for example Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi mine in Mongolia). These newer deposits will push up the global cost curve and be supportive of commodity prices.

quote: Resource stocks also outperformed on the higher commodity prices, with AWE (up 10.1%), Rio Tinto (up 6.6%), BHP (up 5.8%) and Woodside Petroleum (up 4.4%).

headline: Perennial added to Henderson Group as part of strategy to increase offshore earnings exposure
reasoning: Henderson Group was one of the stocks the Trust added to during November as part of a deliberate strategy to increase exposure to companies with significant offshore earnings. This was funded by taking profits in strongly performing domestic resource stocks such as BHP, Rio Tinto, and Aristocrat Leisure.
quote: Proceeds were used to increase our holdings in a number of stocks, including those with significant offshore earnings, such as Henderson Group, Nufarm, Amcor and Resmed.

headline: Western Areas up 28.3% in November as low nickel ore stocks at Chinese ports and Philippine wet season provide positive price catalyst
reasoning: Western Areas, a low-cost nickel producer, benefitted from nickel's 7.0% price rise and improved offtake terms. Low nickel prices earlier in the year, poor weather and Philippine Government production bans all contributed to low nickel ore stocks at Chinese ports. As the Philippine wet season (Oct–Feb) continues, the ore shortage is providing a positive driver for nickel prices. The stock was one of the best contributors to the Trust during the month.
quote: One of the best contributors during the month was low-cost nickel producer Western Areas (up 28.3%), which benefitted from nickel's 7.0% rise and improved terms for its offtake. Low nickel prices earlier in the year, poor weather and Philippine Government production bans have all contributed to low stocks of nickel ore at Chinese ports. As we move into the Philippine wet season (Oct – Feb), that ore shortage is providing a positive driver for nickel prices.

headline: Newcrest fell 13.4% on lower gold price but mine tour impressed Perennial on operating performance
reasoning: Newcrest fell 13.4% in November as the gold price declined 7.7%. During the month, Perennial toured Newcrest's Cadia (NSW) and Lihir (PNG) mines and came away impressed with both operating performance and outlook, suggesting the Trust retains confidence in the company despite the price weakness.
quote: Newcrest (down 13.4%) fell on the lower gold price. During the month, we toured Newcrest's Cadia and Lihir mines, located in NSW and PNG respectively and were impressed with their operating performance and outlook.

headline: Perennial remains underweight healthcare as bond yields rise, sector fell 1.6% in November

headline: Perennial overweight large-cap, low-cost resources companies as fiscal stimulus theme plays out
reasoning: The Trust is positioned with an overweight in large-cap, low-cost, financially-sound resources companies. This is expected to benefit should the US fiscal stimulus theme materialise and commodity demand remains supported. The materials allocation is 15.8% versus the index 16.2%, though energy at 6.7% versus 4.1% index represents a meaningful overweight.
quote: Should this eventuate, the Trust will likely benefit from being overweight in the large-cap, low-cost, financially-sound resources companies as well as in a range of quality industrial and financial companies where we see attractive valuations.

headline: Trump reflation trade drives rotation into cyclicals and commodity prices, with iron ore up 24.6% and hard coking coal up 20.2% in November
reasoning: The US election result triggered a 'Trump reflation' trade, with international markets reacting positively — S&P500 up 3.4%, Nikkei up 5.1%, Shanghai up 4.8%. Iron ore surged 24.6% and hard coking coal rose 20.2%, while oil gained 6.7%. Thermal coal declined 23.7% from recent highs and gold fell 7.7%. The RBA and Federal Reserve both left rates unchanged. The Australian Dollar fell 2 cents to 0.74 US cents.
quote: The key development over the month was the result of the US election. International markets generally reacted positively, with the S&P500 up 3.4%, Nikkei 225 up 5.1% and Shanghai Composite up 4.8%, while the FTSE 100 declined 2.5%. The month saw strong rallies in iron ore (up 24.6%) and hard coking coal (up 20.2%), while oil rose also 6.7%. Thermal coal declined 23.7% from its recent high and gold declined 7.7%.
